headline: Margins expand as Tinder turnaround offsets soft revenue
summary_short: Match Group's Q2 2026 revenue of $853M was down 1.2% y/y as Payers fell 6.0% to 13.3M, but Adjusted EBITDA rose 14.3% y/y to $331M and net income jumped 35.9% to $171M on Tinder's improving engagement trends and Hinge's 22% revenue growth.
summary_long: Revenue's y/y dip reflects a 6% Payer decline to 13.3M, offset by RPP up 6% to $21.13 as pricing outpaced churn. Tinder's turnaround narrowed y/y DAU declines to 4%, the best in 10 quarters, while Hinge grew revenue 22% y/y and expanded into six new European and four Latin American countries. Net income's 36% y/y gain reflects lower cost of revenue (down 16%, to 24% of revenue) and G&A (down 22%), partly offset by higher interest expense on the exchangeable notes. Match repaid $424M of exchangeable notes in June and ended the quarter with $581M cash and $3.6B debt. For Q3, it guides revenue of $885-895M and Adjusted EBITDA of $330-335M, and declared a $0.20/share dividend.
